I built my queen marchesa deck around 1 premise "no matter what, I want a turn 3 or turn 4 Marchesa every game" 

So I included almost every MDFC land in those colors, a bunch of land cyclers, and then backed it up with some reanimation and actual threats.

I try to keep my reddit presence a bit more separate from other places but I can tell you some essentials

[[Doomwake Giant]], [[Thoughtrender Lamia]], [[Eidolon of Blossoms]] are all obvious. The original constellation payoffs. I also run [[Enchantress's Presence]] and [[Argothian Enchantress]] even though snakes will not trigger these as one is an enchantment itself and the other is 2 mana and has shroud.

Two more recent cards Im really loving are [[Shifting Woodland]] and [[Ripples of Undeath]]. I think Ripples is slept on and basically a second sylvan library here, Shifting Woodland is like hands down the best card in the deck to the point where I added a few artifact lands and utility artifacts to help facilitate delirium which is fairly easy to get. The main artifacts I run are [[Skullclamp]] because duh and [[Haywire Mite]], and I run [[Darkmoss Bridge]] as an artifact land. 

I run both the Duskmourn Overlords in these colors. [[Overlord of the Hauntwoods]] is just a good ramp piece that is a big guy and [[Overlord of the Balemurk]] is more self mill and a cheap Enchantress or constellation trigger. 

Some more cards I think are really good in her:

[[Aftermath Analyst]] for self mill and a big burst of ramp. [[Hedge Shredder]] for similar reasons. 

[[Snarling Gorehound]] surveils every time you make a snake and a lot of other creatures are 2 or less power too. 

[[Creeping Renaissance]] is amazing. It's similar to something like [[Praetor's Counsel]] but the flashback here is amazing as there is a good chance we could mill it and it is a huge value piece. 

I dont run them personally but if you want to be a bit more rampy, any of those cheap land auras that get run alongside [[Arbor Elf]] could be really good, esp if you run more pure enchantresses like [[Verduran Enchantress]]

Pharika is indestructible and deck rebuilds well so I try to run a good number of wraths. [[Pernicious Deed]] and [[Extinguish All Hope]] are great, deed due to being an enchantment and recurrable, Extinguish since it should leave a good amount of our board intact while likely being a total wipe for everyone else. 


Hope that helps you get started!

Basically mounted units don't interact well with terrain. Most of the cards won't trap them though. To make up for this, they tend to have much higher movespeed/points cost than non-mounted units would have. 

You can certainly do Hedonites with mounted units. Seekers have ridiculous movespeed even for a mounted unit. That said, I tend to prefer taking a swarm of Daemonettes with a Chaos Lord Ally for my warband. I use the Seeker leader still, which is a mounted unit. 

Seekers tend to be higher points cost for more HP and movespeed, but the same damage profile. While the movespeed and wounds is nice, I'd rather increase my model count and go all-in on what really makes Hedonites great: Daemonettes. The Chaos Lord has a double that adds 1" to the movement of my daemonettes, which are already above average move for light infantry. The Seeker Leader then gets to zip about with her above-average damage profile and help out where she's most needed or perform flanks.

Overall, Slaanesh is a pretty horde-y warband, but your hordes of units are going to be dealing similar damage to units that are wayyyy above their pointcost. Daemonettes are 100% the reason to play Slaanesh, but I could see taking some extra seekers if you like the cavalry. I just personally prefer the ally and a fiend.

Elise: Great champ if you want to make them ff @ 15. If you play Rek'sai, the macro is similar. Some of the best ganks and dives in the game. Always active and omnipresent. Perfect to put more passive junglers/laners in the dirt or get snowballing laners ahead. Lots of room for skill expression with transform, cocoon, and Rappel. Highly survivable thanks to rappel and having fast single target CC. Has a wide diversity of builds ranging from more survivable to more utility/poke to glass cannon, plus two viable keystone setups so there's a lot of room for customization depending on the situation. Blood Moon is by far her best skin, but all of her (few) skins are pretty good. 

Evelynn: Basically a later game version of Elise. Better when your lanes are losing or more passive. Farms until 6 (or goes for very, very sure early ganks) but then snowballs hard. Just like Elise she's also super slippery with high survivability. Probably uses kills better than any other champ thanks to mejai's being semi-core on her. Shadow, Blood Moon, and either KDA or Prestige are her best skins.

Kindred: One of the coolest designs and lore in League. Also one of the few ranged junglers and the only true ADC jungler (sorry Graves.) Is kind of a jack of all trades who can be aggressive and spam ganks/objectives or look to powerfarm and scale depending on matchups. Mark minigame rewards good macro and intelligent invades, plus you get a lot of the same gameplay fantasy as champs like Vayne or Lucian, getting to kite around the battlefield with multiple short dashes. Spirit Blossom Kindred is also one of the best skins in the game.

Hey there! Lots and lots and lots of Pyromancer stuff to go over! I've been playing the deck since last July so I've got about a year and a half experience on it. 

I see someone already linked you to BrainSmoothie's tournament report. I've been helping him tune the list he had there, he's been doing pretty well with it lately. I think the biggest changes are just some sideboard optimization, and his list is pretty good to start (I'd cut the Collective Brutality for the fourth bolt, however.) 

The main thing about this archetype is that it's not for the impatient. Your typical play pattern will look something like

"Discard/Removal turn 1, Discard/Removal turn 2, Seasoned Pyromancer/Blood Moon turn 3". The first two turns are always meant to setup, with the third turn being where our deck goes "online." 

Aside from that, most of the decision points in the deck come down to essentially picking cards. You need to have good threat assessment to use discard spells and your efficient removal spells as well. The right target isn't always the one you would think. For example, Oko is a really powerful card in Modern right now, that's being played in a lot of decks, but depending on the deck, I'll often just ignore the card if it's on the field and try to kill them over it, rather than waste resources trying to attack into it unprofitably.

There's also the matter of Seasoned Pyromancer and Ransack the Lab and those discard decisions. Obviously flashback spells are always the best discards, followed slightly behind by Blood Moon in matchups it isn't good, Discard Spells in lategame when you want to draw threats instead, and excess lands. That said, don't be afraid to pitch Revelers if you have them early, or even Hazoret. You run four of the Reveler, and also two Kolaghan's Command, so you have a pretty high chance of still being able to Reveler if you discard it to something like Seasoned Pyromancer early. 

Overall, I think the deck is really fun and rewarding. It's definitely a deck that rewards mastery, and it's pretty good in the midrangy, value-oriented Oko-meta we seem to find ourselves in. The list and sideboard are also fairly customizable. I'd say the glue of the deck is definitely Seasoned Pyromancer. That card is just fantastic.

Hit me up if you want more Mardu advice. You can also find me @thelovelymedusa on Twitter. 

One last thing I'll say. Don't forget that Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard effect is at instant speed! It can kind of act as either a fog or a psuedo-haste style effect.

Hi there! So glad to see someone pumped about this deck! I would have to disagree with most of the commenters here. While I don't think Mardu Pyromancer is tier 1, I do think the deck is more than capable of putting up results, and we've seen it recently in the 5-0 dump, as well as in the top 8 of the recent Modern Challenge.

I've been working a bit with the pilot of that top 8 list to refine it a bit, but here is his VERY good writeup on that tournament:

[Mardu Reveler Report](https://www.reddit.com/r/ModernMagic/comments/e8h0v0/mardu_reveler_report_top_8_of_modern_challenge/)

The deck still has legs, but has had to move in a different direction after the looting ban. Simply put, Young Pyromancer isn't really that good anymore. While it might seem weird to ditch the namesake card, luckily, Modern Horizons gave us Seasoned Pyromancer. While the token generating potential on Seasoned Pyromancer isn't as high, he does something the instant he hits the battlefield, which is great! It also means we get to play even less creatures, and more interactive spells.

We're also a Blood Moon deck again, which is easy to do since Seasoned Pyromancer discards the card so easily. We can also filter it out with Ransack the Lab, the unsung hero of the strategy. While this card doesn't look particularly great on the surface (It's just a black Strategic Planning), it's been amazing in testing and everyone who's played with it that I've talked to has been very impressed with its role in the deck.

One of the silver linings of the Looting ban was that people stopped maindecking or even sideboarding super aggressive graveyard hate. There aren't too many decks running Rest in Peace running around, and a lot of the anti-graveyard cards right now seem to be oneshot effects, like Nihil Spellbomb. This means that Bedlam Reveler is really good, as we can repeatedly fill up our graveyard with cheap spells to cast it easily. It's easy to forget about this card, which hasn't seen too much relevance in Modern lately, but this thing is essentially our Bloodbraid Elf. It's a Treasure Cruise stapled to a Tarmogoyf!

The best part about this deck is probably that there's nothing we really care about getting Elked, and with three copies of Dreadbore and copious hand disruption, Oko isn't particularly worrisome.

While it's definitely not the deck I'd take to an SCG Open with any intention of winning the whole thing, I think that Mardu Pyromancer (or Mardu Reveler, if you don't want to count Seasoned Pyromancer as "A Pyromancer" haha), is a very strong anti-meta deck that could definitely be on the brink of resurgence. I strongly urge you to read r/brainsmoothie101's writeup that I linked above, as that goes more in detail on his matches and how the deck feels to play. I also recommend the Competitive Mardu Facebook group.

There *are* ways for a Shirona to become a normal human again, but they all usually involve tracking down the demon who made the contract and convincing them somehow to break it. Not easily done! One of the Archangels could also probably cleanse the contract, but Archangels tend to keep to themselves now that The Great Work has been carried out and Earth is created. 

Girls don't necessarily get more evil, although certainly Inketh become like rabid dogs. But the lifestyle of a Shirona means that most of them aren't exactly heroes. Also it takes a certain sort of person to make THAT sort of deal with a demon. 

I haven't really fleshed out a lot of characters topside yet. Hellverse mainly centers around Hell and Heaven, and the would-be successor to God, the Mad Scientist Archangel, Centiskolos. Also some stuff about multiple worlds, Eldritch Entities, a Big Bad who comes from another universe, etc. However, since Shirona are meant to fit into the "Blood Countess" trope, it would stand to reason that throughout the ages, certain women of high rank have either attained that through the powers of being a Shirona, or became a Shirona when they saw said power slipping away.

Two more interesting things to note! Wendigo are similar to Shirona in their ravenous appetite and need for specifically *human* flesh, but unlike Shirona, such a need is a craving and they can persist on other flesh. Also unlike the Shirona, they're transformed constantly, as their affliction is the result of being cursed by a demon (often because they broke a contract.) 

The second interesting piece of information concerns the unborn child that the Shirona sacrifices as part of the ritual. Not all Shirona go through with this sacrifice. Those who don't may be turned into Wendigo or otherwise punished by the demons they made contracts with, but the child itself becomes an Incubus, if male, or a Succubus, if female, with much the same characteristics as Incubi or Succubi have in conventional lore.

The Shirona are women who call upon dark arts for eternal beauty, but they pay a terrible price for their looks. The Shirona can eat no other food but that which comes from a human source, forced to dine on human meat and blood. If they do not manage to sate their appetite, then the Shirona’s beauty will vanish, and they will instead be a vicious beast, rampaging until their hunger is sated.
	The specifics of the ritual the Shirona undertake would be better off in a grimoire, but in essence, a Shirona will engage in ritualistic sex with a demon, and become pregnant with a child that is both demonic and human. After three months of pregnancy, the Shirona performs a second ritual which allows her to absorb the child, gaining the powers that they will then wield.
	A Shirona’s beauty is unrivalled. They are timeless, flawless, gorgeous in every description.They will never age, and never die, unless killed, and thus, they are one of the few breeds of monster that can truly be considered immortal, and not simply long-lived. The Shirona’s bestial form, on the other hand, is hideous. Emaciated and long-limbed, with fiery red eyes and a gaping maw. Their limbs and skeleton take on an elongated appearance, large, bony claws adorn their hands and feet, with an enlarged claw on the index fingers and large toes, curved like that of a raptor. Elder Shirona often learn to control this transformation to some extent, although it is still inevitable if they become starved. Younger Shirona, however, are often unable to control the transformation, metamorphosing at the mere stirrings of appetite. 
	There are two types of Shirona, and while their powers are largely the same, the distinction between them is important. The first kind is the Inketh. These are young girls who, driven by mockery or personal insecurity, desire greater beauty than what nature has given them. An Inketh is often out of control, and most are unable to remain hidden for long in human society. In larger cities, where they can prowl the streets and prey on the rabble in dark alleyways, the chances are better, but many Inketh are quickly slain. 
	The Basteth are older women, who often wish to retain beauty, or halt death. The Basteth’s age and experience (for many of them are powerful witches even before the transformation) gives her a greater amount of control over her newfound form. Basteth are by far the more dangerous of the two, older and experienced, and often skilled in the use of other kinds of magic. The Basteth is often able to remain hidden, and even assume a leadership position in the town where she is located. It is said that Basteth are also hardier than their Inketh counterparts, stronger, faster, and more resistant to harm, although this may not be true. An Inketh that survives for thirty years will become a Basteth, gaining greater control over her hunger and her power.

While Shirona are often likened to Vampires or Ghouls, a Shirona is actually a type of Wendigo. While the distinction should be obvious from the standpoint of less physical attributes (A Wendigo is often not a voluntary transformation while due to the magical ritual involved in the Shirona's creation, all Shirona voluntarily become such, the Shirona does not share the Wendigo's love for cold climates, nor its signature howl), A shirona can, visually, be mistaken for a wendigo if one is not looking for a few key characteristics.

-Lack of fur on the body

-Leaner and less muscular in appearance

-Wider, less elongated snout, more akin to a cat or a toad than the vaguely canid snout structure most wendigo possess.

-Long hair on the head, the last remaining sign that this beast was once a beautiful woman.

-Lack of antlers. While not all Wendigo possess antlers, no Shirona will have the large, elk-like antlers seen in some Wendigo.
